Speed, distance and time

HGV driver

Transport and logistics

\(\displaystyle t = \dfrac{d}{s}\)

Does this run need a legal break?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Lorry drivers must take a 45-minute break after 4½ hours of driving. A 270-mile run at an average of 50 mph (example figures):

  1. Driving time: \(270 \div 50 = 5.4\) hours = 5 h 24 min \((0.4 \times 60 = 24)\).
  2. That's over 4½ hours, so a 45-minute break goes in: 5 h 24 min + 45 min = 6 h 09 min door to door.

The answer: \(270 \div 50 = 5.4\) hours
